en.html:
Before it. We were actually there.

We had circled east, threaded the gaps in their watch, approached, then taken a chance to armor up and fly. Low all the way to the Kubo <ruby>headquarters<rt>headquarters</rt></ruby>.

And not once had anyone intercepted us.

...Too convenient.

Choose a weak point in their defenses, certainly. Even so, warriors flying a few dozen meters above ground must be seen. Surely they must. Someone sees us, reports to headquarters; headquarters orders the air-defense units out; some of those units catch us.

That had been my calculation. Against that degree of resistance, a brief forced breakthrough need not be impossible.

Perhaps even that estimate was too sweet.

Reality was sweeter still. Sugar candy.

So unharmed that our armor seemed almost ridiculous, Ichijou and I stood at our destination. An infiltration I had expected to be punishing, completed with such ease. Why, I did not understand.

...No. I <ruby>had not understood<rt>・・・</rt></ruby>.

Not until we reached Raichou Imagawa's residence, and saw what stood before us.

ja.html:
前に――いるのだった。
　東から回り込み、警戒線の間隙を縫って接近、折を
見て装甲騎航。低高度を保ちつつ公方府を目指した末、

　とうとう何の迎撃も受けることなく。
　
　……出来過ぎであった。

　いかに防備の薄い箇所を狙おうが、数十メートルの
低空を飛ぶ騎影は必ず目視確認される。されない筈が
ない。されれば<ruby>公方府<rt>ヘッドクォーターズ</rt></ruby>へ連絡が行こうし、行けば防空
隊にも指令が下り、その一部は俺達を捕捉するだろう。

　そう考えていた。その程度なら短時間の強行突破も
不可能ではなかろうと。
　それはむしろ、甘い目測であったのかもしれない。

　しかし現実は輪を掛けて甘く、砂糖菓子同然だった。

　装甲姿がいっそ滑稽なほどの無傷ぶりで、俺と一条
は目指した場所へ立っている。
　苛酷を窮めると思われた潜入行がここまでたやすく
成ってしまった理由はわからない。

　……否。わからな<ruby>かった<rt>・・・</rt></ruby>。
　
　あまりに容易な進攻の果て、今川雷蝶の居館へ遂に
到り、その有様を視野に収めるまでは。

en.html:
I entered the devastated residence, <ruby>smoke and dust<rt>smoke and dust</rt></ruby> hanging in the air. Ichijou followed.

Total chaos inside.

Suppose a great army had attacked by surprise and overrun the place at once. Even then, could it have become this?

Damage that could only suggest machine guns fired blindly. A collapsed wall. Before it, an overturned mortar, barrel bent—what was this? Had someone fired a thing like that indoors?

And corpses.

Death and death and death and death, everywhere.

Every one in Rokuhara uniform.

Raichou Imagawa was dead.

Oyumi's Kubo headquarters lay destroyed.

We had done nothing.

We, their enemies, had done absolutely nothing.

So no enemy had destroyed them. War had not killed them.

What had killed and destroyed them, then? What wipes out multitudes, quite apart from war?

A natural disaster.

A great storm, thunder and rain whirling within it. A conflagration spreading on the wind. A tidal wave swallowing the coast. A great eruption, the mountain's fury turning everything around it to hell.

Equal to those.

As sudden. As irresistible. As merciless.

Killing people. Destroying their lives and works. A phenomenon that did only that.

　だから彼らは敵に滅ぼされたのではない。

　雷雨の渦巻く大嵐。風に乗って広がる大火。沿岸を
呑み尽くす大海嘯。山の怒りが周辺全てを地獄に変え

　それらと同等。
　同じように突然で、同じように抗えず、同じように
無慈悲。人を殺す。人の営みを滅ぼす。ただそれだけ
の現象。
